I'll break down the toy car modeling process step by step:

## Step-by-Step Description:

### 1. Create the Main Car Body
- Create a box with dimensions 200x100x100 (length x width x height)
- This will serve as the base shape of the toy car

### 2. Create the Windshield Cutout
- Create a smaller box with dimensions 50x100x50 
- Position this box at the top front edge of the main body
- The box should be aligned so that:
  - It starts from the front face of the car body
  - It covers the full width (100 units)
  - It extends 50 units back from the front
  - It extends 50 units down from the top

### 3. Subtract Windshield from Body
- Use a boolean difference operation to subtract the windshield box from the main body
- This creates the angled windshield effect

### 4. Create the Wheels
- Create four cylinders, each with:
  - Radius: 25 units
  - Height/thickness: 10 units
  - Orientation: cylinders should be oriented horizontally (along the width axis)

### 5. Position the Wheels
- Place wheels at the four bottom corners of the car body
- Each wheel should be positioned so that it's half-embedded into the body
- This means the center of each cylinder should be at the bottom edge of the car body
- Wheel positions:
  - Front-left wheel
  - Front-right wheel  
  - Rear-left wheel
  - Rear-right wheel

### 6. Union the Wheels with the Body
- Use boolean union operations to merge each wheel with the car body
- This creates the semicylindrical protrusions as specified

The final result will be a toy car with an angled windshield cutout and four wheels that appear as semicircular protrusions from the bottom of the car body.
